chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Washsha', from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him saying: 'When the Negus proposed to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) the hand of Umm Habiba (Amnat bint Abi Sufyan), may Allah curse him, and he married her, he invited people to food and said: "Indeed, among the traditions of the Messengers is providing food at the time of marriage."'

key_terms.آمِنَةَ بِنْتَ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ: Amnat bint Abi Sufyan (Umm Habiba), wife of the Prophet
key_terms.النَّجَاشِي: The Negus, the King of Abyssinia

ai.seo_question: What is the prophetic tradition regarding food and feasting during marriage ceremonies according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) narrates that when the Negus married Umm Habiba to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), he hosted a feast, establishing the Sunnah of providing food during marriage ceremonies as a practice of the Prophets. This hadith, found in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the social dimension of Nikah in Shia jurisprudence, linking marital celebration to the prophetic tradition of communal sharing and generosity.
